comment: Relying solely on clinician workflows to drive adoption and ensure treatment adherence is often insufficient. Without transactional visibility, patients remain passive subjects rather than active drivers of their own care loops. In chronic disease management (such as hypertension or diabetes), activating the patient as an active participant introduces a vital layer of systemic accountability and catches errors before they cause irreversible harm.

public.text: Relying solely on clinician workflows to drive adoption and ensure treatment adherence is often insufficient. Without transactional visibility, patients remain passive subjects rather than active drivers of their own care loops. In chronic disease management (such as hypertension or diabetes), activating the patient as an active participant introduces a vital layer of systemic accountability and catches errors before they cause irreversible harm.
public.suggestedRevision: Add to adoption layer guidance: “The DPI-H framework should recommend patient-visible loop closure and real-time transaction receipts as a core component of the adoption layer. Rather than treating patient portals as optional, passive viewing panes, the guidelines should encourage architectures that automatically send active transactional notifications to patients—such as alerts when a chronic disease prescription is filled or missed, or confirmations when a critical referral loop has closed.”
